latest_release.name: v0.50.0
latest_release.body:
# Atlantis v0.50.0

v0.50.0 fixes one **high-severity** security advisory and is a **breaking release** for anyone using the API or drift detection, which now require an explicit experiment opt-in.

## Upgrade checklist

- [ ] **API or drift detection users:** add the matching names to the new `experiments` setting before upgrading (see below). Without them, Atlantis refuses to start if `api-secret` or a drift flag is set, and `/api/*` routes return HTTP 404.
- [ ] **`team_authz.command` users on Bitbucket Server or Azure DevOps:** upgrade promptly (GHSA-7v86-958w-j7hj). No configuration change is needed.
- [ ] **Everyone else:** no action required.

## Security

### GHSA-7v86-958w-j7hj: VCS repository name run as shell source in the external team-allowlist command (High, CVSS 7.2)

When `team_authz.command` is set in the server-side repo config, Atlantis built the external command as one string and ran it with `sh -c`. The repository full name was not quoted. On Bitbucket Server (project display name) and Azure DevOps (organization, project and repository names), a crafted name could run arbitrary commands on the Atlantis server with its environment and credentials, or make the check print `pass` and bypass the authorization decision.

The fix passes the Atlantis command name, the repository full name and each `owner/team` value as separate arguments, so the shell never parses them. The configured `command` and `args` are still run by `sh`, so commands that embed their own arguments keep working, and the argument order your script sees is unchanged.

- **Affected:** v0.49.0 and earlier, only with `team_authz.command` configured, on Bitbucket Server or Azure DevOps. GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Bitbucket Cloud repository names cannot contain shell metacharacters.
- **Exploiting it requires** permission to name or rename a repository or project on the VCS host, which is a project administrator by default.
- **Docs:** [Repo and project permissions](https://www.runatlantis.io/docs/repo-and-project-permissions.html#external-command) now describe how arguments are passed and how configured `args` shift their positions.

Reported by EZO Labs Security (@superbot-helper).

### Dependency and image security updates

- Docker image: Alpine OpenSSH `10.3_p1-r2` for CVE-2026-123158 (#7065), Alpine `curl` 8.23.0-r0 (#7027), Alpine Git 2.54.1-r0 (#7093), Alpine base 3.24.4 (#7076, #7104), git-lfs 3.8.1 (#7080).
- Go modules: `golang.org/x/crypto` v0.59.0 (#7087), `golang.org/x/net` v0.62.0 (#7044), `github.com/klauspost/compress` v1.20.2 (#7066).
- Docs site: `minimatch` 11 and overrides for vulnerable docs-site dependencies (#7045, #7021).

## Breaking changes

### API and drift detection now require an experiment opt-in (#7030)

The API (`/api/plan`, `/api/apply`, `/api/locks`) and drift detection are experimental features, and a new `experiments` server setting now has to grant each one:

- `api` permits the command and lock routes.
- `drift-detection` permits the drift routes.

**What changes on upgrade:**

- Atlantis **refuses to start** if `api-secret`, `enable-drift-detection` or `enable-drift-remediation` is set without the matching experiment.
- Routes without permission return **HTTP 404**, including `GET /api/locks`, which used to be public.

**To keep your current behavior,** add the experiments you use:

```sh
atlantis server --experiments=api,drift-detection
# or
ATLANTIS_EXPERIMENTS=api,drift-detection
```

```yaml
experiments:
  - api
  - drift-detection
```

For a drift-only installation, use only `drift-detection`. Before rolling back to v0.49.0 or earlier, remove the `experiments` setting, because older binaries don't recognize it. See [Experiments](https://www.runatlantis.io/docs/experiments.html) for details.

## Bug fixes

- Atlantis no longer answers its own comments: error, help and command-suggestion replies are suppressed for comments written by the configu

# Atlantis [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/runatlantis/atlantis.svg)](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/releases/latest) [![SuperDopeBadge](./runatlantis.io/public/hightower-super-dope.svg)](https://twitter.com/kelseyhightower/status/893260922222813184) [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis) [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis) [![Slack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join-Atlantis%20Community%20Slack-red)](https://slack.cncf.io/) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/runatlantis/atlantis) [![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/9428/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/9428)



Terraform Pull Request Automation

- [Get involved](#get-involved) - [Resources](#resources) - [What is Atlantis?](#what-is-atlantis) - [What does it do?](#what-does-it-do) - [Why should you use it?](#why-should-you-use-it) - [Stargazers over time](#stargazers-over-time) ## Get involved Help shape Atlantis! Share feedback, discuss ideas, report issues, or contribute code and documentation. - **Community meetings:** Join the conversation at an [Atlantis community meeting](https://zoom-lfx.platform.linuxfoundation.org/meetings/atlantis). - **Slack:** Join [CNCF Slack](https://slack.cncf.io/) and find **#atlantis** for questions and feedback, or **#atlantis-contributors** to discuss ideas and contributions. - **Issues:** [Report a bug or suggest an improvement](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/issues). - **Contributing:** See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started. ## Resources * How to get started: [www.runatlantis.io/guide](https://www.runatlantis.io/guide) * Full documentation: [www.runatlantis.io/docs](https://www.runatlantis.io/docs) * Download the latest release: [github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/releases/latest](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/releases/latest) ## What is Atlantis? A self-hosted golang application that listens for Terraform pull request events via webhooks. ## What does it do? Runs `terraform plan`, `import`, `apply` remotely and comments back on the pull request with the output. ## Why should you use it? * Make Terraform changes visible to your whole team. * Enable non-operations engineers to collaborate on Terraform. * Standardize your Terraform workflows. ## Stargazers over time [![Stargazers over time](https://starchart.cc/runatlantis/atlantis.svg)](https://starchart.cc/runatlantis/atlantis)
